claim: Chromosome segregation depends on the kinetochore, the machine that establishes force-bearing attachments between DNA and spindle microtubules.
source: Chromosome segregation depends on the kinetochore, the machine that establishes force-bearing attachments between DNA and spindle microtubules.
evidence: This is a foundational statement about kinetochore function supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Kinetochores are formed every cell cycle via a highly regulated process that requires coordinated assembly of multiple subcomplexes on specialized chromatin.
source: Kinetochores are formed every cell cycle via a highly regulated process that requires coordinated assembly of multiple subcomplexes on specialized chromatin.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about kinetochore assembly.

claim: An assay was developed to assemble kinetochores de novo using centromeric DNA and budding yeast extracts.
source: To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, we developed an assay to assemble kinetochores de novo using centromeric DNA and budding yeast extracts.
evidence: This is the primary methodological contribution of the manuscript, supported by the experimental data presented throughout.

claim: Assembly is enhanced by mitotic phosphorylation of the Dsn1 kinetochore protein.
source: Assembly is enhanced by mitotic phosphorylation of the Dsn1 kinetochore protein and generates kinetochores capable of binding microtubules.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and quantitative mass spectrometry results in Figure 3C.

claim: The assembled kinetochores are capable of binding microtubules.
source: Assembly is enhanced by mitotic phosphorylation of the Dsn1 kinetochore protein and generates kinetochores capable of binding microtubules.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 4B showing microtubule binding assays.

claim: The CENP-T pathway becomes essential for viability when the Mis12 pathway is crippled by defects in Dsn1 phosphorylation.
source: Although the CENP-T pathway is non-essential in yeast, we demonstrate that it becomes essential for viability and Ndc80c recruitment when the Mis12 pathway is crippled by defects in Dsn1 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by genetic data in Figure 7A showing synthetic lethality and assembly data in Figure 7C.

claim: The CENP-T pathway becomes essential for Ndc80c recruitment when the Mis12 pathway is crippled by defects in Dsn1 phosphorylation.
source: Although the CENP-T pathway is non-essential in yeast, we demonstrate that it becomes essential for viability and Ndc80c recruitment when the Mis12 pathway is crippled by defects in Dsn1 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by assembly assay data in Figure 7C showing reduced Ndc80 recruitment in the double mutant.

claim: Aneuploidy is a hallmark of birth defects and cancers.
source: Chromosomes must be accurately segregated to daughter cells during cell division to avoid aneuploidy, a hallmark of birth defects and cancers (Pfau and Amon, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Pfau and Amon, 2012.

claim: Faithful chromosome segregation relies on the attachment of chromosomes to spindle microtubules via the kinetochore.
source: Faithful segregation relies on the attachment of chromosomes to spindle microtubules via the kinetochore, a conserved protein complex that assembles at centromeres (Yamagishi et al., 2014; Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yamagishi et al., 2014 and Musacchio and Desai, 2017.

claim: The kinetochore is a conserved protein complex that assembles at centromeres.
source: Faithful segregation relies on the attachment of chromosomes to spindle microtubules via the kinetochore, a conserved protein complex that assembles at centromeres (Yamagishi et al., 2014; Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yamagishi et al., 2014 and Musacchio and Desai, 2017.

claim: Kinetochores must track dynamically growing and shrinking microtubule tips.
source: Kinetochores must track dynamically growing and shrinking microtubule tips, monitor for erroneous kinetochore-microtubule attachments, and serve as the platform for the spindle assembly checkpoint (Biggins, 2013; Joglekar and Kukreja, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Biggins, 2013 and Joglekar and Kukreja, 2017.

claim: Kinetochores monitor for erroneous kinetochore-microtubule attachments.
source: Kinetochores must track dynamically growing and shrinking microtubule tips, monitor for erroneous kinetochore-microtubule attachments, and serve as the platform for the spindle assembly checkpoint (Biggins, 2013; Joglekar and Kukreja, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Biggins, 2013 and Joglekar and Kukreja, 2017.

claim: Kinetochores serve as the platform for the spindle assembly checkpoint.
source: Kinetochores must track dynamically growing and shrinking microtubule tips, monitor for erroneous kinetochore-microtubule attachments, and serve as the platform for the spindle assembly checkpoint (Biggins, 2013; Joglekar and Kukreja, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Biggins, 2013 and Joglekar and Kukreja, 2017.

claim: The kinetochore is a megadalton protein structure composed of many subcomplexes.
source: To carry out these many functions, the kinetochore is a highly regulated, megadalton protein structure composed of many subcomplexes (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The underlying mechanisms that regulate kinetochore assembly are not well understood.
source: Although these subcomplexes must faithfully assemble onto the centromere every cell cycle, the underlying mechanisms that regulate kinetochore assembly are not well understood.
evidence: This statement reflects the knowledge gap that motivates the study.

claim: Kinetochores are built on a specialized centromeric chromatin structure in which canonical histone H3 is replaced with CENP-A.
source: Kinetochores are built on a specialized centromeric chromatin structure, in which canonical histone H3 is replaced with a centromere-specific variant, CENP-A (Earnshaw and Rothfield, 1985; Salmon and Bloom, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Earnshaw and Rothfield, 1985 and Salmon and Bloom, 2017.

claim: Most eukaryotes have complex 'regional' centromeres composed of repetitive DNA stretches with interspersed CENP-A- and H3-containing nucleosomes.
source: Most eukaryotes have complex 'regional' centromeres composed of repetitive DNA stretches with interspersed CENP-A- and H3-containing nucleosomes (Blower et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Blower et al., 2002.

claim: The constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) binds to centromeric chromatin to form the inner kinetochore.
source: The constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) binds to centromeric chromatin to form the inner kinetochore and serve as the scaffold for outer kinetochore assembly, which mediates microtubule attachment (Foltz et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Foltz et al., 2006.

claim: The CCAN serves as the scaffold for outer kinetochore assembly, which mediates microtubule attachment.
source: The constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) binds to centromeric chromatin to form the inner kinetochore and serve as the scaffold for outer kinetochore assembly, which mediates microtubule attachment (Foltz et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Foltz et al., 2006.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is a key microtubule-binding site within the kinetochore.
source: The Ndc80 complex ('Ndc80c') is a key microtubule-binding site within the kinetochore, because it directly mediates attachment and recruits additional attachment factors, such as the Ska complex in vertebrates and its functional ortholog Dam1 in fungi (Cheeseman et al., 2006; DeLuca et al., 2005; Maure et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2017; Lampert et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations including Cheeseman et al., 2006; DeLuca et al., 2005; Maure et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2017; Lampert et al., 2013.

claim: The Ndc80 complex directly mediates microtubule attachment and recruits additional attachment factors.
source: The Ndc80 complex ('Ndc80c') is a key microtubule-binding site within the kinetochore, because it directly mediates attachment and recruits additional attachment factors, such as the Ska complex in vertebrates and its functional ortholog Dam1 in fungi (Cheeseman et al., 2006; DeLuca et al., 2005; Maure et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2017; Lampert et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations including Cheeseman et al., 2006; DeLuca et al., 2005; Maure et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2017; Lampert et al., 2013.

claim: There are two parallel kinetochore receptors for Ndc80c: the Mis12 complex and CENP-T.
source: Interestingly, there are two parallel kinetochore receptors for Ndc80c: the Mis12 complex ('Mis12c') and CENP-T (Maskell et al., 2010; Malvezzi et al., 2013; Schleiffer et al., 2012; Gascoigne et al., 2011; Nishino et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations including Maskell et al., 2010; Malvezzi et al., 2013; Schleiffer et al., 2012; Gascoigne et al., 2011; Nishino et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2012.

claim: Mis12c interacts with the KNL1 and Ndc80 complexes to create a larger network called KMN.
source: Mis12c interacts with the KNL1 and Ndc80 complexes to create a larger network called KMN (KNL1-Mis12-Ndc80) (Cheeseman et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cheeseman et al., 2006.

claim: CENP-T is a histone-fold domain containing protein.
source: CENP-T, a histone-fold domain containing protein, recruits Ndc80c via the same interaction surface on the Ndc80 complex that binds Mis12c (Nishino et al., 2013; Schleiffer et al., 2012; Malvezzi et al., 2013; Hori et al., 2008; Dimitrova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations including Nishino et al., 2013; Schleiffer et al., 2012; Malvezzi et al., 2013; Hori et al., 2008; Dimitrova et al., 2016.

claim: CENP-T recruits Ndc80c via the same interaction surface on the Ndc80 complex that binds Mis12c.
source: CENP-T, a histone-fold domain containing protein, recruits Ndc80c via the same interaction surface on the Ndc80 complex that binds Mis12c (Nishino et al., 2013; Schleiffer et al., 2012; Malvezzi et al., 2013; Hori et al., 2008; Dimitrova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations including Nishino et al., 2013; Schleiffer et al., 2012; Malvezzi et al., 2013; Hori et al., 2008; Dimitrova et al., 2016.

claim: Mis12c and CENP-T each contribute to Ndc80c recruitment in vivo.
source: Although Mis12c and CENP-T each contribute to Ndc80c recruitment in vivo (Malvezzi et al., 2013; Gascoigne et al., 2011), it has been unclear why cells employ two competing receptors for Ndc80c and whether the CENP-T protein functions as a histone at centromeres.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Malvezzi et al., 2013 and Gascoigne et al., 2011.

claim: Pre-formed nucleosomal arrays incubated in Xenopus egg extracts assemble microtubule-binding elements.
source: For example, pre-formed nucleosomal arrays incubated in Xenopus egg extracts assemble microtubule-binding elements that allowed the identification of events required to initiate kinetochore assembly (Guse et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Guse et al., 2011.

claim: The binding selectivity of some kinetochore proteins for CENP-A nucleosomes over H3 nucleosomes was determined by reconstituting the entire linkage between the CENP-A nucleosome and KMN.
source: Furthermore, the binding selectivity of some kinetochore proteins for CENP-A nucleosomes (over H3 nucleosomes) was recently determined by reconstituting the entire linkage between the CENP-A nucleosome and KMN (Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Weir et al., 2016.

claim: Budding yeast have a simple 'point' centromere that is defined by a ~125 bp specific DNA sequence.
source: To do this, we used budding yeast because they have a simple 'point' centromere that is defined by a ~ 125 bp specific DNA sequence and a single microtubule attachment site per chromosome (Winey et al., 1995; Biggins, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Winey et al., 1995 and Biggins, 2013.

claim: Budding yeast have a single microtubule attachment site per chromosome.
source: To do this, we used budding yeast because they have a simple 'point' centromere that is defined by a ~ 125 bp specific DNA sequence and a single microtubule attachment site per chromosome (Winey et al., 1995; Biggins, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Winey et al., 1995 and Biggins, 2013.

claim: The kinetochore subcomplexes and functions are largely conserved in budding yeast.
source: The kinetochore subcomplexes and functions are largely conserved, including the specialized chromatin structure containing CENP-ACse4 that serves as the platform for kinetochore assembly.
evidence: This reflects established knowledge about conservation of kinetochore components.

claim: Dual pathways for Ndc80 recruitment are used in yeast.
source: Additionally, dual pathways for Ndc80 recruitment are used in yeast, although the CENP-T ortholog, Cnn1, is not essential for viability (Schleiffer et al., 2012; Bock et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schleiffer et al., 2012 and Bock et al., 2012.

claim: The CENP-T ortholog Cnn1 is not essential for viability in yeast.
source: Additionally, dual pathways for Ndc80 recruitment are used in yeast, although the CENP-T ortholog, Cnn1, is not essential for viability (Schleiffer et al., 2012; Bock et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schleiffer et al., 2012 and Bock et al., 2012.

claim: CENP-TCnn1 contributes to kinetochore function because mutants display increased chromosome loss.
source: However, CENP-TCnn1 contributes to kinetochore function because mutants display increased chromosome loss, and the tethering of CENP-TCnn1 imparts partial stability to acentric minichromosomes via Ndc80 recruitment (Malvezzi et al., 2013; Bock et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Malvezzi et al., 2013 and Bock et al., 2012.

claim: Tethering of CENP-TCnn1 imparts partial stability to acentric minichromosomes via Ndc80 recruitment.
source: However, CENP-TCnn1 contributes to kinetochore function because mutants display increased chromosome loss, and the tethering of CENP-TCnn1 imparts partial stability to acentric minichromosomes via Ndc80 recruitment (Malvezzi et al., 2013; Bock et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Malvezzi et al., 2013 and Bock et al., 2012.

claim: CENP-TCnn1 localization to kinetochores peaks in mitosis as a result of phosphoregulation.
source: In yeast, CENP-TCnn1 localization to kinetochores peaks in mitosis as a result of phosphoregulation (Schleiffer et al., 2012; Bock et al., 2012), but it is unclear why its recruitment is cell cycle regulated and whether this affects the Mis12 pathway of Ndc80 recruitment.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schleiffer et al., 2012 and Bock et al., 2012.

claim: Every protein assayed bound specifically to centromeric DNA within 30 min of assembly.
source: Within 30 min of assembly, every protein assayed bound specifically to centromeric DNA (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Inner kinetochore components are generally saturated within 30 min of assembly.
source: Inner kinetochore components are generally saturated within 30 min, while outer kinetochore proteins require longer to reach saturation.
evidence: This is inferred from the time course data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Outer kinetochore proteins require longer than 30 min to reach saturation.
source: Inner kinetochore components are generally saturated within 30 min, while outer kinetochore proteins require longer to reach saturation.
evidence: This is inferred from the time course data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 39 out of 49 core kinetochore proteins were detected at higher coverage levels on CEN3 DNA relative to control DNA templates.
source: We detected 39 out of 49 core kinetochore proteins at higher coverage levels on CEN3 DNA relative to either ampC DNA or CEN3mut DNA (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the mass spectrometry data presented in Table 1.

claim: CENP-ACse4 was specifically enriched on CEN3 DNA.
source: In support of centromeric nucleosome assembly, CENP-ACse4 was specifically enriched on CEN3 DNA.
evidence: This is supported by the mass spectrometry data in Table 1.

claim: Components from all known kinetochore subcomplexes were detected on CEN3 DNA.
source: Importantly, we detected components from all known kinetochore subcomplexes on CEN3 DNA, including the CENP-TCnn1 protein.
evidence: This is supported by the mass spectrometry data in Table 1.

claim: CENP-TCnn1 protein was detected on CEN3 DNA.
source: Importantly, we detected components from all known kinetochore subcomplexes on CEN3 DNA, including the CENP-TCnn1 protein.
evidence: This is supported by the mass spectrometry data in Table 1.

claim: All kinetochore complexes assemble on centromeric DNA under the conditions developed.
source: Together, these data suggest that all kinetochore complexes assemble on centromeric DNA under the conditions we developed.
evidence: This is inferred from the mass spectrometry data in Table 1.

claim: The assembly reaction was completely inhibited on CEN3 DNA in ndc10-1 extracts.
source: Similar to the negative controls, the assembly reaction was completely inhibited on the CEN3 DNA in the ndc10-1 extracts (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the immunoblot data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The assembly reaction is initiated by CBF3, consistent with the requirements for assembly in vivo.
source: Together, these data indicate that the assembly reaction is initiated by CBF3, consistent with the requirements for assembly in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the ndc10-1 mutant data in Figure 1D and known requirements in vivo.

claim: Kinetochore assembly in vivo requires a CENP-A nucleosome.
source: Kinetochore assembly in vivo requires a CENP-A nucleosome, so we tested whether CENP-ACse4 requires its chaperone HJURPScm3 for deposition (Camahort et al., 2007; Shivaraju et al., 2011; Stoler et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Camahort et al., 2007; Shivaraju et al., 2011; Stoler et al., 2007.

claim: Ndc10 associated with CEN3 DNA in the presence or absence of HJURPScm3.
source: As expected for the most upstream protein in the assembly pathway, Ndc10 associated with CEN3 DNA in the presence or absence of HJURPScm3.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 2A.

claim: CENP-ACse4 and all other CCAN components assayed no longer associated with CEN3 when HJURPScm3 was depleted.
source: However, CENP-ACse4 and all other CCAN components assayed no longer associated with CEN3 when HJURPScm3 was depleted (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 2A.

claim: The strict requirement for CENP-ACse4 recruitment by its chaperone suggests that CENP-ACse4 is forming a functional nucleosome in vitro.
source: This strict requirement for CENP-ACse4 recruitment by its chaperone suggests that CENP-ACse4 is forming a functional nucleosome in vitro.
evidence: This is inferred from the HJURPScm3 depletion data in Figure 2A.

claim: Centromeric nucleosomes can be detected in the surrounding pericentromeric region in vivo.
source: Centromeric nucleosomes can be detected in the surrounding pericentromeric region in vivo (Coffman et al., 2011; Lawrimore et al., 2011; Wisniewski et al., 2014), leading to debate about whether a single CENP-ACse4 nucleosome is sufficient for kinetochore assembly (Aravamudhan et al., 2013; Furuyama and Biggins, 2007; Wisniewski et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Coffman et al., 2011; Lawrimore et al., 2011; Wisniewski et al., 2014.

claim: CENP-ACse4 levels were similar on both 180 bp and 250 bp templates.
source: CENP-ACse4 levels were similar on both templates, and the entire kinetochore formed in both cases (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 2B.

claim: The entire kinetochore formed on both 180 bp and 250 bp templates.
source: CENP-ACse4 levels were similar on both templates, and the entire kinetochore formed in both cases (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 2B.

claim: A single, well-positioned centromeric nucleosome is sufficient for kinetochore assembly in the absence of surrounding pericentromeric DNA.
source: Together, these data suggest that a single, well-positioned centromeric nucleosome is sufficient for kinetochore assembly in the absence of surrounding pericentromeric DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the data in Figure 2B showing assembly on 180 bp templates.

claim: Kinetochore assembly occurs during S phase in budding yeast.
source: Kinetochore assembly is regulated during the cell cycle and occurs during S phase in budding yeast (Kitamura et al., 2007; Pearson et al., 2004), although it isn't clear whether this reflects a requirement for active DNA replication or another S phase event.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kitamura et al., 2007 and Pearson et al., 2004.

claim: There are dynamic changes in kinetochore composition during mitosis.
source: During mitosis, there are dynamic changes in kinetochore composition and CENP-TCnn1 levels at kinetochores peak due to phosphoregulation (Schleiffer et al., 2012; Bock et al., 2012; Dhatchinamoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schleiffer et al., 2012; Bock et al., 2012; Dhatchinamoorthy et al., 2017.

claim: CENP-TCnn1 levels at kinetochores peak during mitosis due to phosphoregulation.
source: During mitosis, there are dynamic changes in kinetochore composition and CENP-TCnn1 levels at kinetochores peak due to phosphoregulation (Schleiffer et al., 2012; Bock et al., 2012; Dhatchinamoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schleiffer et al., 2012; Bock et al., 2012; Dhatchinamoorthy et al., 2017.

claim: Assembly is least efficient in extracts from cells arrested in G1.
source: Assembly is least efficient in extracts from cells arrested in G1 and most efficient in S phase and mitosis (Figure 3A), consistent with cell cycle regulation that occurs in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 3A.

claim: Assembly is most efficient in S phase and mitosis.
source: Assembly is least efficient in extracts from cells arrested in G1 and most efficient in S phase and mitosis (Figure 3A), consistent with cell cycle regulation that occurs in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 3A.

claim: The CENP-TCnn1 pathway is noticeably enhanced in kinetochores assembled from mitotic extracts.
source: As expected, the CENP-TCnn1 pathway is noticeably enhanced in kinetochores assembled from mitotic extracts.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 3A.

claim: Aurora B-mediated phosphorylation of Dsn1 promotes the interaction between Mis12c and CENP-CMif2.
source: A conserved mitotic phosphorylation event that promotes kinetochore assembly is Aurora B-mediated phosphorylation of Dsn1, which promotes the interaction between Mis12c and the inner kinetochore protein CENP-CMif2 (Akiyoshi et al., 2013a; Kim and Yu, 2015; Yang et al., 2008; Dimitrova et al., 2016; Petrovic et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Akiyoshi et al., 2013a; Kim and Yu, 2015; Yang et al., 2008; Dimitrova et al., 2016; Petrovic et al., 2016.

claim: The dsn1-2D assembled kinetochores showed a strong enrichment for outer kinetochore proteins beginning with the Mis12 complex.
source: While the innermost CCAN proteins were present at equivalent levels, the dsn1-2D assembled kinetochores showed a strong enrichment for outer kinetochore proteins beginning with the Mis12 complex itself when assayed by immunoblotting and mass spectrometry (Figure 3B and Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by the immunoblot data in Figure 3B and mass spectrometry data in Table 2.

claim: There was a strong enrichment of outer kinetochore proteins (3- to 7-fold enrichment) in the dsn1-2D assembled kinetochores.
source: Similar to the immunoblot analysis, there was a strong enrichment of outer kinetochore proteins (3- to 7-fold enrichment) in the dsn1-2D assembled kinetochores while the CCAN levels were similar to WT assembled kinetochores (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative mass spectrometry data in Figure 3C.

claim: The CCAN levels were similar in WT and dsn1-2D assembled kinetochores.
source: Similar to the immunoblot analysis, there was a strong enrichment of outer kinetochore proteins (3- to 7-fold enrichment) in the dsn1-2D assembled kinetochores while the CCAN levels were similar to WT assembled kinetochores (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative mass spectrometry data in Figure 3C.

claim: The assembly assay in vitro reflects requirements known for assembly in vivo and is sensitive to critical post-translational modifications.
source: Together, these data indicate that our assembly assay in vitro reflects requirements known for assembly in vivo and is sensitive to critical post-translational modifications.
evidence: This is inferred from the dsn1-2D phosphomimetic data in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: Ndc80 levels are not noticeably reduced by the loss of CENP-TCnn1 in vivo.
source: It has been unclear how CENP-TCnn1 facilitates kinetochore assembly in yeast, because Ndc80 levels are not noticeably reduced by the loss of CENP-TCnn1in vivo (Bock et al., 2012; Schleiffer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bock et al., 2012 and Schleiffer et al., 2012.

claim: Ndc80 and KNL1Spc105 levels are slightly reduced in a cnn1Δ extract.
source: We therefore performed the assembly assay in a cnn1Δ extract and found that Ndc80 and KNL1Spc105 levels are slightly reduced, suggesting that CENP-TCnn1 contributes to Ndc80 recruitment (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 6.

claim: CENP-TCnn1 contributes to Ndc80 recruitment.
source: We therefore performed the assembly assay in a cnn1Δ extract and found that Ndc80 and KNL1Spc105 levels are slightly reduced, suggesting that CENP-TCnn1 contributes to Ndc80 recruitment (Figure 6).
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly assay data in Figure 6.

claim: Ndc80 assembly is considerably reduced in an extract from which dsn1-AID had been degraded.
source: We next compared this to the role of Mis12c in Ndc80 recruitment by performing the assay in an extract from which dsn1-AID had been degraded. Here, Ndc80 assembly is considerably reduced but not absent.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 6.

claim: Ndc80 recruitment is abolished in a cnn1Δ dsn1-AID double mutant.
source: To test whether the residual Ndc80 is due to CENP-TCnn1, we analyzed assembly from a cnn1Δ dsn1-AID double mutant and found that Ndc80 recruitment is abolished.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 6.

claim: The de novo assay uses both pathways of assembly.
source: Together, these data show that the de novo assay uses both pathways of assembly and that CENP-TCnn1 contributes to Ndc80 recruitment independently of the Mis12 complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly assay data in Figure 6.

claim: CENP-TCnn1 contributes to Ndc80 recruitment independently of the Mis12 complex.
source: Together, these data show that the de novo assay uses both pathways of assembly and that CENP-TCnn1 contributes to Ndc80 recruitment independently of the Mis12 complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly assay data in Figure 6.

claim: Mis12c is the major Ndc80 receptor in budding yeast.
source: Although CENP-TCnn1 contributes to Ndc80 recruitment, Mis12c is clearly the major Ndc80 receptor in budding yeast (Schleiffer et al., 2012; Bock et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schleiffer et al., 2012 and Bock et al., 2012.

claim: Mis12c is essential for viability while CENP-TCnn1 is non-essential.
source: Consistent with this, Mis12c is essential for viability while CENP-TCnn1 is non-essential, leading to the question of why yeast have retained the CENP-TCnn1 pathway.
evidence: This reflects established knowledge about the essentiality of these pathways.

claim: Yeast cells lacking the Aurora B phosphorylation sites (dsn1-2A) are inviable due to low Dsn1 protein expression.
source: Although yeast cells lacking the Aurora B phosphorylation sites (dsn1-2A) are inviable due to low Dsn1 protein expression, mutating an additional Cdk1 site (serine 264) restores protein levels and viability (dsn1-3A) (Akiyoshi et al., 2013a; Akiyoshi et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Akiyoshi et al., 2013a and Akiyoshi et al., 2013b.

claim: Mutating an additional Cdk1 site (serine 264) restores protein levels and viability in dsn1-3A.
source: Although yeast cells lacking the Aurora B phosphorylation sites (dsn1-2A) are inviable due to low Dsn1 protein expression, mutating an additional Cdk1 site (serine 264) restores protein levels and viability (dsn1-3A) (Akiyoshi et al., 2013a; Akiyoshi et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Akiyoshi et al., 2013a and Akiyoshi et al., 2013b.

claim: dsn1-3A weakens the interaction between Mis12c and CENP-CMif2.
source: Because dsn1-3A weakens the interaction between Mis12c and CENP-CMif2, we postulated that this linkage is not essential due to compensation by the CENP-TCnn1 pathway.
evidence: This is based on known effects of the dsn1-3A mutation.

claim: There is synthetic lethality between dsn1-3A and cnn1Δ.
source: Consistent with this, there was synthetic lethality between dsn1-3A and cnn1Δ (Figure 7A), indicating that CENP-TCnn1 becomes essential when the Mis12 pathway is misregulated.
evidence: This is supported by the genetic data in Figure 7A.

claim: CENP-TCnn1 becomes essential when the Mis12 pathway is misregulated.
source: Consistent with this, there was synthetic lethality between dsn1-3A and cnn1Δ (Figure 7A), indicating that CENP-TCnn1 becomes essential when the Mis12 pathway is misregulated.
evidence: This is inferred from the synthetic lethality data in Figure 7A.

claim: Deletions of CENP-KMcm22 and CENP-NChl4 are synthetically lethal with dsn1-3A.
source: To further test this, we crossed dsn1-3A to additional mutants in the CENP-TCnn1 pathway (deletions of CENP-KMcm22 and CENP-NChl4). These deletions are also synthetically lethal with dsn1-3A (Figure 7A), indicating that the entire CENP-TCnn1 pathway is essential for viability when the interaction between Dsn1 and CENP-CMif2 is crippled by a lack of Aurora B phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by the genetic data in Figure 7A.

claim: The entire CENP-TCnn1 pathway is essential for viability when the interaction between Dsn1 and CENP-CMif2 is crippled by a lack of Aurora B phosphorylation.
source: These deletions are also synthetically lethal with dsn1-3A (Figure 7A), indicating that the entire CENP-TCnn1 pathway is essential for viability when the interaction between Dsn1 and CENP-CMif2 is crippled by a lack of Aurora B phosphorylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the synthetic lethality data in Figure 7A.

claim: A CENP-TCnn1 deletion has synthetic phenotypes with a CENP-CMif2 mutant that cannot bind to Mis12c.
source: These data are consistent with previous observations that a CENP-TCnn1 deletion has synthetic phenotypes with a CENP-CMif2 mutant that cannot bind to Mis12c and with a temperature sensitive allele of the Mis12 complex component NNF1 (Bock et al., 2012; Hornung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bock et al., 2012 and Hornung et al., 2014.

claim: A CENP-TCnn1 deletion has synthetic phenotypes with a temperature sensitive allele of NNF1.
source: These data are consistent with previous observations that a CENP-TCnn1 deletion has synthetic phenotypes with a CENP-CMif2 mutant that cannot bind to Mis12c and with a temperature sensitive allele of the Mis12 complex component NNF1 (Bock et al., 2012; Hornung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bock et al., 2012 and Hornung et al., 2014.

claim: The mcm22-AID dsn1-3A double mutant was inviable when auxin was added.
source: The mcm22-AID dsn1-3A double mutant was inviable when auxin was added (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by the growth assay data in Figure 7B.

claim: The dsn1-3A extracts showed a considerable decrease in Ndc80 assembly as well as the other KMN components, Dsn1 and KNL1Spc105.
source: As expected, the dsn1-3A extracts showed a considerable decrease in Ndc80 assembly as well as the other KMN components, Dsn1 and KNL1Spc105, and that Ndc80 recruitment was further reduced in the dsn1-3A mcm22-AID double mutant (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 7C.

claim: Ndc80 recruitment was further reduced in the dsn1-3A mcm22-AID double mutant.
source: As expected, the dsn1-3A extracts showed a considerable decrease in Ndc80 assembly as well as the other KMN components, Dsn1 and KNL1Spc105, and that Ndc80 recruitment was further reduced in the dsn1-3A mcm22-AID double mutant (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 7C.

claim: KNL1Spc105 assembly appears unaffected by CENP-KMcm22 degradation.
source: Despite this reduction in Ndc80, KNL1Spc105 assembly appears unaffected by CENP-KMcm22 degradation, suggesting that the CENP-TCnn1 pathway may specifically recruit Ndc80 and not the full KMN network.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly assay data in Figure 7C.

claim: The CENP-TCnn1 pathway may specifically recruit Ndc80 and not the full KMN network.
source: Despite this reduction in Ndc80, KNL1Spc105 assembly appears unaffected by CENP-KMcm22 degradation, suggesting that the CENP-TCnn1 pathway may specifically recruit Ndc80 and not the full KMN network.
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly assay data in Figure 7C.

claim: The kinetochores were scattered in the dsn1-3A mcm22-AID double mutant cells indicating a defect in establishing normal kinetochore-microtubule attachments.
source: While the majority of WT cells exhibited a normal bi-lobed distribution of kinetochores, the kinetochores were scattered in the double mutant cells indicating a defect in establishing normal kinetochore-microtubule attachments (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by the microscopy data in Figure 7D.

claim: The CENP-TCnn1 pathway is required to recruit critical levels of Ndc80 complex to kinetochores to mediate proper kinetochore-microtubule attachments when the centromere recruitment of the Mis12c is compromised by a defect in Aurora B phosphorylation.
source: Together, our data suggest that the CENP-TCnn1 pathway is required to recruit critical levels of Ndc80 complex to kinetochores to mediate proper kinetochore-microtubule attachments when the centromere recruitment of the Mis12c is compromised by a defect in Aurora B phosphorylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data in Figure 7.

claim: Similar assays incubating yeast centromeric DNA in extracts were previously developed but none achieved assembly of the outer kinetochore.
source: Although similar assays incubating yeast centromeric DNA in extracts were previously developed, none achieved assembly of the outer kinetochore (Ohkuni and Kitagawa, 2011; Sandall et al., 2006; Sorger et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ohkuni and Kitagawa, 2011; Sandall et al., 2006; Sorger et al., 1994.

claim: By altering the extract conditions, all known kinetochore subcomplexes were assembled on a centromeric DNA template.
source: By altering the extract conditions, we were able to assemble all known kinetochore subcomplexes on a centromeric DNA template.
evidence: This is supported by the mass spectrometry data in Table 1.

claim: The assembly of all kinetochore proteins depends on the CBF3 complex.
source: First, the assembly of all kinetochore proteins depends on the CBF3 complex, which is required to initiate assembly in vivo (Poddar et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by the ndc10-1 mutant data in Figure 1D and citation to Poddar et al., 2004.

claim: CENP-A association with the template requires its chaperone.
source: Second, CENP-A association with the template requires its chaperone (Camahort et al., 2007; Shivaraju et al., 2011; Stoler et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by the HJURPScm3 depletion data in Figure 2A and citations to Camahort et al., 2007; Shivaraju et al., 2011; Stoler et al., 2007.

claim: Histone H2A, H2B, and H4 are present, suggesting that a centromeric nucleosome forms on the DNA.
source: Histone H2A, H2B, and H4 are also present, suggesting that a centromeric nucleosome forms on the DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the mass spectrometry data in Table 1.

claim: DNA templates capable of wrapping a single centromeric nucleosome efficiently assemble kinetochores.
source: We found that DNA templates capable of wrapping a single centromeric nucleosome efficiently assemble kinetochores, consistent with recent work showing that KMN can link to a single centromeric nucleosome (Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by the assembly data in Figure 2B and citation to Weir et al., 2016.

claim: Pericentromeric chromatin is not required for kinetochore assembly in vitro.
source: In addition, these data demonstrate that pericentromeric chromatin is not required for kinetochore assembly in vitro, although it contributes to kinetochore function in vivo (Bloom, 2014).
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly data in Figure 2B and citation to Bloom, 2014.

claim: Outer kinetochore protein recruitment depends on the inner kinetochore proteins.
source: Third, outer kinetochore protein recruitment depends on the inner kinetochore proteins (Gascoigne and Cheeseman, 2011; Hara and Fukagawa, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gascoigne and Cheeseman, 2011 and Hara and Fukagawa, 2018.

claim: Kinetochore assembly is more efficient in extracts made from cells arrested in S phase or mitosis.
source: Fourth, kinetochore assembly is more efficient in extracts made from cells arrested in S phase or mitosis.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly data in Figure 3A.

claim: Active DNA replication is not a strict requirement for kinetochore assembly.
source: Because replication cannot occur in extracts without sequential kinase treatment (Heller et al., 2011), our assay also shows that active DNA replication is not a strict requirement for kinetochore assembly.
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly data and citation to Heller et al., 2011.

claim: All CCAN subcomplexes analyzed are required for CENP-TCnn1 kinetochore localization in vitro.
source: We found that all CCAN subcomplexes analyzed are required for CENP-TCnn1 kinetochore localization in vitro, which is generally consistent with work analyzing its localization in human cells (Carroll et al., 2010; Basilico et al., 2014; Samejima et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2015; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016; Logsdon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by the assembly data in Figure 5 and citations to Carroll et al., 2010; Basilico et al., 2014; Samejima et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2015; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016; Logsdon et al., 2015.

claim: CENP-TCnn1 does not have intrinsic DNA binding activity under the assay conditions.
source: Regardless, these data are consistent with the conclusion that CENP-TCnn1 does not have intrinsic DNA binding activity under our assay conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly data in Figure 5.

claim: CENP-S/XMhf1/2 are not specifically binding to centromeric DNA.
source: In addition, we did not detect CENP-S/XMhf1/2 specifically binding to centromeric DNA, suggesting they are not yeast kinetochore components.
evidence: This is inferred from the mass spectrometry data in Table 1.

claim: The OA complex is the bifurcation point of the Mis12c and CENP-TCnn1 assembly pathways.
source: We propose that the OA complex is the bifurcation point of the Mis12c and CENP-TCnn1 assembly pathways, because the CENP-QOkp1 mutant perturbed the assembly of both KMN and CENP-POCtf19-Mcm21, while the CCAN subcomplexes downstream of CENP-CMif2 and OA specifically altered only the CENP-TCnn1 pathway.
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly data in Figure 5.

claim: The CENP-TCnn1 recruitment pathway is comprised of the CENP-PO (CM complex), CENP-HIK, and CENP-LN complexes.
source: The CENP-TCnn1 recruitment pathway is therefore comprised of the CENP-PO (CM complex), CENP-HIK, and CENP-LN complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly data in Figure 5 and illustrated in Figure 7E.

claim: All of the non-essential, conserved yeast kinetochore proteins are specific to the CENP-T pathway.
source: We note that all of the non-essential, conserved yeast kinetochore proteins are specific to the CENP-T pathway, providing an explanation for why the yeast kinetochore contains both essential and non-essential proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the pathway analysis and known essentiality data.

claim: In human cells, the CENP-T pathway recruits Ndc80 both directly and indirectly.
source: In human cells, the CENP-T pathway recruits Ndc80 both directly and indirectly. The CENP-T protein directly binds to two Ndc80 complexes and recruits a third via a phospho-regulated interaction with a Mis12 complex that is also bound to an Ndc80 complex (Huis In 't Veld et al., 2016; Rago et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Huis In 't Veld et al., 2016 and Rago et al., 2015.

claim: CENP-T knockdown in human cells results in severely decreased Mis12 and KNL1 complexes at kinetochores.
source: CENP-T knockdown in human cells results in severely decreased Mis12 and KNL1 complexes at kinetochores (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Kim and Yu, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gascoigne et al., 2011 and Kim and Yu, 2015.

claim: There is no evidence for the recruitment of KMN by CENP-TCnn1 in budding yeast.
source: In contrast, we did not find evidence for the recruitment of KMN by CENP-TCnn1 in budding yeast, consistent with data showing that recombinant CENP-TCnn1 does not interact with recombinant Mis12 complex in vitro (Schleiffer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is inferred from the assembly data and citation to Schleiffer et al., 2012.

claim: The CCAN mutants that specifically inhibit the CENP-TCnn1 pathway did not alter Mis12 or KNL1Spc105 assembly.
source: The CCAN mutants we assayed that specifically inhibit the CENP-TCnn1 pathway did not alter Mis12 or KNL1Spc105 assembly.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly data in Figure 5.

claim: A lack of linkage between CENP-TCnn1 and the Mis12 complex in yeast may explain why CENP-TCnn1 is non-essential and does not contribute to spindle checkpoint signaling.
source: A lack of linkage between CENP-TCnn1 and the Mis12 complex in yeast may also explain why CENP-TCnn1 is non-essential and does not contribute to spindle checkpoint signaling (Schleiffer et al., 2012; Bock et al., 2012).
evidence: This is inferred from the data and citations to Schleiffer et al., 2012 and Bock et al., 2012.

claim: Yeast cells are viable when the conserved phosphorylation sites that promote Mis12c localization are mutated.
source: The Mis12 pathway is responsible for the majority of Ndc80 recruitment in yeast, so it is surprising that yeast cells are viable when the conserved phosphorylation sites that promote Mis12c localization are mutated (Akiyoshi et al., 2013a; Kim and Yu, 2015; Yang et al., 2008; Dimitrova et al., 2016; Petrovic et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Akiyoshi et al., 2013a; Kim and Yu, 2015; Yang et al., 2008; Dimitrova et al., 2016; Petrovic et al., 2016.

claim: Cells lacking Dsn1 phosphorylation are viable because they use the CENP-TCnn1 pathway to assemble a functional kinetochore.
source: Here, we discovered these cells are viable because they use the CENP-TCnn1 pathway to assemble a functional kinetochore.
evidence: This is inferred from the synthetic lethality and assembly data in Figure 7.

claim: When the CENP-TCnn1 pathway is eliminated in cells lacking Dsn1 phosphorylation, Ndc80 levels are significantly reduced and kinetochores are defective in making normal attachments to microtubules in vivo.
source: When the CENP-TCnn1 pathway is eliminated in cells lacking Dsn1 phosphorylation, Ndc80 levels are significantly reduced and kinetochores are defective in making normal attachments to microtubules in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by the assembly data in Figure 7C and microscopy data in Figure 7D.

claim: The CENP-TCnn1 assembly pathway is required to recruit critical levels of Ndc80 when the function of the Mis12c pathway is reduced.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the CENP-TCnn1 assembly pathway is required to recruit critical levels of Ndc80 when the function of the Mis12c pathway is reduced.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data in Figure 7.

claim: CENP-TCnn1 kinetochore levels peak at anaphase.
source: CENP-TCnn1 kinetochore levels peak at anaphase (Bock et al., 2012; Dhatchinamoorthy et al., 2017), which is the time when Aurora B-mediated phosphorylation of kinetochore proteins is reversed by phosphatase activity.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bock et al., 2012 and Dhatchinamoorthy et al., 2017.

claim: The anaphase enrichment of CENP-TCnn1 might increase the load-bearing potential of kinetochore-microtubule attachments by recruiting more Ndc80.
source: Therefore, the anaphase enrichment of CENP-TCnn1 might not only increase the load-bearing potential of kinetochore-microtubule attachments by recruiting more Ndc80, but also reinforce kinetochore stability when Aurora B-mediated phosphorylation of Dsn1 is removed.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the timing of CENP-TCnn1 enrichment and its function.

claim: The anaphase enrichment of CENP-TCnn1 might reinforce kinetochore stability when Aurora B-mediated phosphorylation of Dsn1 is removed.
source: Therefore, the anaphase enrichment of CENP-TCnn1 might not only increase the load-bearing potential of kinetochore-microtubule attachments by recruiting more Ndc80, but also reinforce kinetochore stability when Aurora B-mediated phosphorylation of Dsn1 is removed.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the timing of CENP-TCnn1 enrichment and its function.

claim: Switching to an Ndc80-recruiting pathway that does not recruit KMN may help silence the spindle assembly checkpoint, as KNL1 is the critical scaffold for the SAC.
source: In addition, switching to an Ndc80-recruiting pathway that does not recruit KMN may also help silence the spindle assembly checkpoint, as KNL1 is the critical scaffold for the SAC.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the functional significance of the CENP-T pathway.

claim: The assembly assay is complementary to a previously developed assembly method using preassembled chromatin templates and frog egg extracts.
source: Our assay is complementary to a previously developed assembly method using preassembled chromatin templates and frog egg extracts (Guse et al., 2011), but provides the advantage of being genetically tractable.
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work with citation to Guse et al., 2011.

claim: The assembly assay provides the advantage of being genetically tractable.
source: Our assay is complementary to a previously developed assembly method using preassembled chromatin templates and frog egg extracts (Guse et al., 2011), but provides the advantage of being genetically tractable.
evidence: This is a stated advantage of the developed method.

claim: The assembly assay will be useful for directly examining the role of other post-translational modifications in kinetochore assembly.
source: In the future, our assembly assay will be useful for directly examining the role of other post-translational modifications in kinetochore assembly.
evidence: This is a prospective statement about future applications of the method.

claim: The assembly assay will provide a method to assess the biophysical and structural properties of each Ndc80 recruitment pathway.
source: In addition, it will provide a method to assess the biophysical and structural properties of each Ndc80 recruitment pathway to better understand how cells maintain kinetochore-microtubule attachments to ultimately ensure accurate chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is a prospective statement about future applications of the method.
